meta.title: Computer Science & Systems Curriculum — Source-Grounded Edition
meta.policy: Required exercises are official source work; synthesized mastery targets and agent supplements are explicitly labeled.

labels.OFFICIAL: Appears in the linked source course/material.
labels.SYNTHESIZED_TARGET: Expected mastery inferred from official topics; not an official assignment.
labels.SUPPLEMENTAL: Optional agent-generated work, never required by default.
labels.ACCESS_BLOCKED: Official item cannot be accessed and must not be silently replaced.

CS61A.course: UC Berkeley CS 61A — Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
CS61A.access: Public schedule, readings, labs, discussions, homework, projects and many solutions. Some institutional quiz/submission systems require enrollment.
CS61A.role: Programming abstraction, recursion, data abstraction, interpreters and SQL.

CS61B.access: Public lectures, worksheets, homework and project specifications. Some autograding/submission services may require enrollment.
CS61B.role: Java, software construction, data structures and graph algorithms.

CS70.course: UC Berkeley CS 70 — Discrete Mathematics and Probability Theory
CS70.access: Public notes, discussion worksheets, homework PDFs and many solutions.
CS70.role: Proof, induction, graph theory, number theory, counting and probability.

MITMCS.access: Free textbook, lecture videos, problem sets, exams and downloadable course materials.
MITMCS.role: A stable open sequence for proofs, state machines, asymptotics, graphs, counting and probability.

MIT6006.access: Free lectures, notes, recitations, assignments and exams.
MIT6006.role: Algorithm modeling, correctness, graph algorithms and dynamic programming.

CS61C.course: UC Berkeley CS 61C — Great Ideas in Computer Architecture
CS61C.access: Public schedule, slides, discussions, labs and project specifications. Some submissions/autograders require enrollment.
CS61C.role: C, RISC-V, logic, datapaths, pipelining, caches, parallelism and virtual memory.

OSTEP.access: Free chapters and source-code homework simulators.
OSTEP.role: Processes, concurrency, virtual memory and persistence.

CS162.course: UC Berkeley CS 162 — Operating Systems and System Programming
CS162.access: Public lecture slides, discussion worksheets, homework and project specifications. Enrolled-course academic-integrity restrictions still apply; do not ask an agent for assignment solutions.
CS162.role: Operating-system abstractions, synchronization, scheduling, virtual memory, file systems and distributed systems.

CMU15445.course: Carnegie Mellon 15-445/645 — Intro to Database Systems
CMU15445.access: Public lecture notes/slides, homework links and BusTub project specifications. Submission infrastructure may require enrollment.
CMU15445.role: Storage, indexes, query execution, optimization, transactions and recovery.

CS144.course: Stanford CS 144 — Introduction to Computer Networking
CS144.access: Public checkpoint specifications and starter repository; some current lecture videos may require Stanford access, while archived videos/materials may be public.
CS144.role: Byte streams, TCP receiver/sender, network interfaces and IP routing.

CS161.access: Public schedule, textbook chapters and discussion worksheets. Gradescope homework may not be public. Never request project solutions.
CS161.role: Security principles, memory safety, cryptography, web and network security.

CS161TEXT.role: Stable reading companion to the archived CS 161 schedule.

MIT65840.access: Public schedule, papers, reading questions and five Go lab specifications. Submission is institutional; local tests are included in starter code.
MIT65840.role: MapReduce, RPC, Raft, replicated key/value services and sharding.

MIT6033.access: Free readings, critiques, design-project material and communication guidance.
MIT6033.role: System-design method, design writing, modularity, reliability and security.

SRE.role: SLIs/SLOs, monitoring, overload, reliability and operations.
